requirements.text: Homepage loads a real, populated seed listing (description, status) — not lorem ipsum, not blank.
The non-binding/novelty disclaimer is woven into the homepage hero headline copy itself.
The public offers list is sorted by amount descending, with ties broken by earliest submission using a server-assigned persistence timestamp, not client-submitted time.
The offer form rejects negative, zero, and non-numeric amounts and enforces a maximum around $10,000,000.
The offer form enforces explicit character caps on the alias and story fields.
A submission-time content filter rejects clearly abusive input while accepting legitimate playful submissions.
Content-filter rejections show an actionable, specific reason, never a generic 'rejected' message.
A clear, visible non-binding disclaimer appears before any offer or payment submission step (in addition to the hero headline).
The demo checkout has no field capable of accepting a real payment card number or CVV — every field is decorative, pre-filled fake, or structurally incapable of accepting a real PAN.
The checkout/payment step is explicitly labeled demo/simulated, and no flow claims a real charge succeeded.
A 'submitted' confirmation state appears only after the offer is actually persisted — never shown optimistically before persistence completes.

If the checkout animation completes visually but the backend persistence write fails, a distinct, tested error state appears with a clear retry action — the success/reorder spectacle never completes and then reveals failure afterward.
A newly submitted offer appears in the sorted public list with a visible animated reorder transition, not a generic success toast.
The leaderboard reorder includes an aria-live announcement of the rank/position change alongside the visual transition.
The listing has a visible report/flag control that gives instant client-facing confirmation when used.
Every individual offer has a visible report/flag control that gives instant client-facing confirmation when used.
The report/flag control enforces a per-device cap of one report per item.
An offer that crosses 3 reports is automatically hidden from the public list (soft-removed, recoverable in the data store, never hard-deleted).
Repeat offer submissions from the same visitor are soft-rate-limited (device-local) without permanently blocking legitimate repeat submissions.
A freshly created/zero-offer listing shows a designed empty state (icon, copy, CTA), never a blank or 'no data' view.
No screen requires real personal data about an actual minor — only placeholder-safe fields (due month/year, alias, short story) are collected, on the seed listing and any offer.
No passively-collected visitor data (IP address, user agent, or similar) is ever logged, displayed, or exported anywhere in the product.
All primary screens fully support light and dark mode.
All primary screens render correctly on mobile and desktop with no overlapping or clipped text.

The offers/leaderboard view is verified against adversarial-length data — a 60-character alias, three offers tied at the same amount, and a $9,999,999 offer — with no text collision, in both light and dark mode.
No screen gates core functionality behind sign-in; there is no account/login system anywhere in the app.
After submitting an offer, the visitor sees a personal shareable result card (rank + brag line) summarizing their submission.
There is no multi-user marketplace (create-your-own-listing or browse/discovery page) — the app ships as a single personal listing only.
